scope.text: Introductory economics; markets for goods and services; all other demand determinants held constant
scope.basis: as-stated for ceteris paribus; broader scope inferred

text: A rise in price of a good or service almost always decreases the quantity demanded; conversely, a fall in price increases the quantity demanded. Economists call this inverse relationship the law of demand, assuming all other variables that affect demand are held constant.
notes: Status empirical: source states 'almost always' and explicitly notes ceteris paribus. Not a definitional identity.
